summary: Updates RFC 3405 by removing references to the IETF tree from the procedure for getting a URI scheme added to the URI.ARPA zone. It is a small process change to registration rules, published as a Best Current Practice.

eli5.summary: A small tidy-up of the paperwork rules for adding a new kind of web address prefix to a special directory.

questions: how to register a uri scheme in uri.arpa
what did rfc 8958 change in rfc 3405
what is the ietf tree for uri schemes
which uri schemes can be added to uri.arpa
subtitle: A one-paragraph fix that stops URI.ARPA registrations from requiring a URI tree that no longer exists.

tldr.problem: RFC 3405 says URI.ARPA registrations must be in the IETF tree of URI schemes, but the tree system was discontinued, so the requirement cannot be met.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8958 removes the IETF-tree requirement and says every registration in URI.ARPA MUST now be for a scheme with a permanent registration under BCP 35.
tldr.outcome: The rule for getting a scheme into URI.ARPA now points at the current registration process. It is a Best Current Practice that updates RFC 3405.

today: RFC 8958 is a Best Current Practice and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It updates RFC 3405.

sections.title: The Problem With the Old Rule
sections.content:
Part Five of the Dynamic Delegation Discovery System (DDDS), RFC 3405, describes how assignments are made in URI.ARPA. It requires that registrations be in the IETF tree of URI registrations.

Trees of URI scheme names were defined in RFC 2717 but discontinued by RFC 4395 and its successors. The current process in BCP 35 (RFC 7595) therefore has no way to register within that tree, so the requirement could not be satisfied.
sections.eli5: An old rule asked for something that no longer exists, like asking for a library card from a library that closed. Nobody could follow it.

sections.title: The Updated Requirement
sections.content:
This document removes the normative requirement from RFC 3405 for registrations in URI.ARPA to be from the IETF URI tree. In its place, all registrations in URI.ARPA MUST now be for schemes that are permanent registrations, as described in BCP 35.

That is the whole change. The document uses the RFC 2119 and RFC 8174 key words only when they appear in capitals.
sections.eli5: The new rule says: only names that are fully and permanently signed up can be added. That is something people can actually do.

sections.title: Instructions to IANA
sections.content: The RFC states that the entire document is updated instructions to IANA. There is no separate list of actions: the changed requirement in the previous section is the instruction.
sections.eli5: The people who keep the list get the new rule and use it from now on.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: This update does not change the security considerations in RFC 3405. Those still apply as written.
sections.eli5: Nothing about safety changes. The old safety notes still stand.
